step1_figure.description: Figure 11.9 shows the transistor-level schematic of the CMOS inverter composed of pull-up PMOS (M2) and pull-down NMOS (M1) connected between VDD and ground with common input and output terminals. Figure 11.7 (page 336) presents the corresponding short-channel DC sweep setup.

switching_point_voltage.description: DC input voltage at which the output voltage equals the input voltage (Vin = Vout = VSP)

equation.formula: VSP = (sqrt(beta_n / beta_p) * VTHN + (VDD - VTHP)) / (1 + sqrt(beta_n / beta_p))
equation.explanation: Derived by equating NMOS and PMOS saturation currents at Vin = Vout = VSP.
equation.assumptions: Both MOSFETs operate in saturation; square-law model applies.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Depending on PMOS-to-NMOS width ratio (2:1 to 3:1), VSP shifts close to VDD/2 (0.9 V).

peak_crossing_current.description: Maximum short-circuit current drawn from VDD when both NMOS and PMOS are simultaneously on during switching

equation.explanation: Peak current occurs at Vin = VSP when both transistors are saturated conducting the maximum cross-conduction current.
equation.assumptions: Square-law saturation model without velocity saturation.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Velocity saturation in 130 nm devices slightly lowers peak current compared to ideal long-channel square-law.

output_high_voltage.description: Steady-state output voltage when the input is logic low (0 V)

equation.explanation: With Vin = 0 V, NMOS is cut off and PMOS pulls output directly to VDD.
equation.assumptions: No static resistive load to ground; negligible junction leakage.

sky130_expected.reasoning: CMOS logic achieves full rail-to-rail high level.

output_low_voltage.description: Steady-state output voltage when the input is logic high (VDD)

equation.explanation: With Vin = VDD, PMOS is cut off and NMOS pulls output directly to GND.
equation.assumptions: No static resistive load to VDD; negligible junction leakage.

sky130_expected.reasoning: CMOS logic achieves full rail-to-rail low level.

input_low_voltage.description: Maximum input voltage recognized as a valid logic low, defined where dVout/dVin = -1

equation.formula: VIL = Vin when d(Vout)/d(Vin) = -1 with Vout near VOH
equation.explanation: Unity-gain point on the VTC marking transition from stable logic low to high-gain region.
equation.assumptions: Standard definition of digital noise margins.

sky130_expected.calculation: For VDD = 1.8 V and VTH = 0.42 V, transition occurs near VIL ≈ VTHN + (VDD - |VTHP| - VTHN)/(1 + beta_n/beta_p) ≈ 0.65 V.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Typically sits slightly above NMOS threshold voltage.

input_high_voltage.description: Minimum input voltage recognized as a valid logic high, defined where dVout/dVin = -1

equation.formula: VIH = Vin when d(Vout)/d(Vin) = -1 with Vout near VOL
equation.explanation: Unity-gain point on the VTC marking transition from high-gain region to stable logic high.
equation.assumptions: Standard definition of digital noise margins.

sky130_expected.calculation: Transition out of high gain occurs when PMOS leaves saturation near VIH ≈ VDD - |VTHP| - 0.3 V ≈ 1.05 V.

noise_margin_low.description: Noise margin for logic low signals

equation.explanation: Maximum spurious low-level signal voltage that does not cause invalid logic evaluation.
equation.assumptions: VOL is zero for CMOS inverter.

sky130_expected.reasoning: With ideal NML = VDD/2 = 0.9 V, realistic value is around 0.65 V due to finite gain.

noise_margin_high.description: Noise margin for logic high signals

equation.explanation: Maximum spurious drop in high-level signal voltage that does not cause invalid logic evaluation.
equation.assumptions: VOH is VDD for CMOS inverter.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Slightly asymmetric with NML depending on PMOS sizing.

propagation_delay_hl.description: High-to-low output propagation delay measured from 50% Vin to 50% Vout

equation.explanation: Time required for NMOS channel resistance to discharge load and parasitic capacitance from 50% VDD.
equation.assumptions: NMOS modeled by average effective resistance Rn.

sky130_expected.calculation: For Ctot ≈ 10 fF and Rn ≈ 1 / (un*Cox * (W/L) * (VDD - VTHN)) ≈ 1 / (270e-6 * (1/0.15) * 1.38) ≈ 400 ohm; tpHL ≈ 0.7 * 3.4k * 10f = 24 ps (with effective Rn ~ 3.4 k-ohm).
sky130_expected.reasoning: Dominated by effective on-resistance and load capacitance.

propagation_delay_lh.description: Low-to-high output propagation delay measured from 50% Vin to 50% Vout

equation.explanation: Time required for PMOS channel resistance to charge load and parasitic capacitance to 50% VDD.
equation.assumptions: PMOS modeled by average effective resistance Rp.

sky130_expected.calculation: With PMOS sized Wp = 2*Wn, effective Rp ≈ Rn ≈ 3.4 k-ohm; tpLH ≈ 0.7 * 3.4k * 10f = 24 ps.
sky130_expected.reasoning: PMOS hole mobility is lower, matched by wider device.

dynamic_power.description: Average dynamic power dissipated when switching at clock frequency fclk

equation.explanation: Energy dissipated per cycle (Ctot * VDD^2) multiplied by switching frequency.
equation.assumptions: Dominant capacitive charging dissipation; input transitions rail-to-rail.

sky130_expected.calculation: For Ctot = 10 fF, VDD = 1.8 V, fclk = 500 MHz (period T = 2 ns): Pavg = 10e-15 * (1.8)^2 * 500e6 = 16.2 uW.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Includes capacitive power plus short-circuit switching dissipation.

power_delay_product.description: Energy-delay product representing energy consumed per switching event

equation.explanation: Figure of merit quantifying trade-off between power dissipation and switching speed.
equation.assumptions: Pavg evaluated over one clock cycle.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Expressed in Joules (energy per switching cycle).

step3_testbench.description: Comprehensive ngspice testbench for Baker Ch11 CMOS Inverter measuring DC transfer characteristics (VOH, VOL, VSP, VIL, VIH, NMH, NML, Icross_peak) and transient switching behavior (tpHL, tpLH, dynamic power, PDP).
step3_testbench.spice:
* CMOS Inverter Testbench - Baker Chapter 11
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

* DUT parameters
.param W_xm1 = 1.0u
.param L_xm1 = 0.15u
.param W_xm2 = 2.0u
.param L_xm2 = 0.15u

* DUT Netlist
xm1 Vout Vin 0 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm1} l={L_xm1}
Vin Vin 0 0
VDD VDD 0 1.8
xm2 Vout Vin VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w={W_xm2} l={L_xm2}

* Output capacitive load (interconnect + fanout)
Cload Vout 0 10f

.control
save all

* ==========================================
* 1. DC Sweep Analysis for VTC and Noise Margins
* ==========================================
dc Vin 0 1.8 0.001

* Rail voltages
meas dc voh find v(Vout) at=0.0
meas dc vol find v(Vout) at=1.8

* Switching point voltage VSP where Vout = Vin
meas dc vsp when v(Vout)=v(Vin)

* Peak crossing current from VDD during switching
let id_vdd = -i(VDD)
meas dc icross_peak max id_vdd

* Unity gain points dVout/dVin = -1 for VIL and VIH
let gain = deriv(v(Vout))
meas dc vil when gain=-1 fall=1
meas dc vih when gain=-1 rise=1

* Noise margins
let nmh = voh - vih
let nml = vil - vol

print vsp icross_peak voh vol vil vih nmh nml

* ==========================================
* 2. Transient Analysis for Switching Delays and Power
* ==========================================
alter @vin[pulse] = [ 0 1.8 0.2n 50p 50p 1n 2.2n ]
tran 1p 4.4n

* Propagation delays (50% to 50%)
meas tran tphl trig v(Vin) val=0.9 rise=1 targ v(Vout) val=0.9 fall=1
meas tran tplh trig v(Vin) val=0.9 fall=1 targ v(Vout) val=0.9 rise=1

* Dynamic power over one complete cycle (0.2ns to 2.4ns)
let inst_pwr = -i(VDD) * 1.8
meas tran pavg avg inst_pwr from=0.2n to=2.4n

* Power Delay Product
let pdp = pavg * (tphl + tplh)
print tphl tplh pavg pdp

quit
.endc
.end
